scope: Twelve approved object-recognition scenes and six ambiguous comparisons. This is a partial library review, not a complete audit.

items.imageAlt: A red apple, a curved yellow banana, and a round orange, separated on a produce counter.
items.reviewedScenario: At the fresh-fruit display, a shopper sees apple, banana, and orange and compares banana with the other options.
items.reason: Objects are clearly separated and recognizable at phone size. The text supplies the shopper action; the picture supports object recognition, without asserting an unpictured action.

items.reviewedScenario: At the morning produce stall, a shopper sees grape, strawberry, and watermelon and chooses watermelon for breakfast.

items.reviewedScenario: At the morning produce stall, a shopper sees mulberry, boysenberry, and acai berry and chooses boysenberry for breakfast.

items.reviewedScenario: In the grocery aisle, a shopper sees tangerine, mandarin, and clementine and puts clementine into a reusable bag.

items.reviewedScenario: At the neighbourhood produce stall, a shopper sees parsnip, ginger, and yam and chooses parsnip for tonight's meal.

items.reviewedScenario: In the grocery aisle, a shopper sees rapini, napa cabbage, and red cabbage and puts rapini into the basket.
